messages:
anika: Heads-up — prepping a catalog switchover for nova-13b-v3 tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Wanted to share a dependency matrix and a proposed safety-hold flow before we submit the deploybot job.

deploy-bot: Deploy window reserved by @anika for 2024-06-15 03:00 UTC → 03:30 UTC. Run ID: DB-1729. Reaction :white_check_mark:.

maria: Thanks — can you post the dependency matrix here? I want to confirm which services need prewarm and which need pinning.

leo: Quick matrix (service -> model variant priority / notes):
```
ui-search     -> nova-13b-v3 (primary), nova-13b-v2 (fallback, pin EU 24h)
reranker     -> nova-13b-quant (primary), nova-6b (fallback, no pin)
chat-api      -> nova-13b-v3 (primary), small-chat (fallback)
batch-embed   -> embed-13b-v3 (primary), embed-7b-quant (fallback)
```
Notes: reranker latency sensitivity — don't unpin reranker variants during the first 2h. Prewarm routing caches ~30m before flip.

aj: Strong +1 on the reranker hold. Proposal: safety-hold that blocks the enable step if 95p latency increases >15% in the first 10m post-cutover. Who owns the rollback?

oncall-sre: SRE will own automated rollback trigger. Suggested policy:
- Metric: reranker 95p latency and chat-api 99p error rate
- Window: 10m sampling, threshold >15% lat bump OR error-rate >0.5%
- Action: immediate traffic pin to previous variant + notify channel and start manual rollback runbook.

anika: Good. Also proposing an explicit pin plan for EU customers: keep nova-13b-v2 pinned for 24h for EU region (reason: regulatory customers and slower canary coverage). After 24h, auto-unpin if no regressions.

maria: Add release notes link and evals checklist to the deploy job. We need: perf smoke, prompt-set sanity for top-50 prompts, and embedding similarity spot-check. Link: https://go/releases/nova-13b-v3-preflight

leo: Also adding fallback ordering preference for the catalog entry: primary -> quantized variant -> smaller model. That ensures graceful degradation at the runtime level. Documented in catalog policy field `fallback_order`.

aj: One more operational ask — if SLOs are marginal during the canary, we should route 20% of traffic to dedicated capacity (reserved pool) to avoid cascading latency on shared hosts. Ops can toggle this flag in the deploy job.

oncall-sre: We will add a transient circuit-breaker with TTL=10m for services that show >10% tail latency change during canary. Circuit-breaker triggers fallback variant and reduces retries.

anika: Action items: 1) @leo add dependency matrix to the runbook file and the deploy job metadata (done after this thread). 2) @maria attach release notes + eval checklist to DB-1729. 3) @oncall-sre configure automated rollback thresholds and circuit-breaker. 4) @aj confirm dedicated-capacity toggle is available for this run.

maria: I updated DB-1729 metadata with the release notes link and checklists. Deploy job now includes `prewarm=30m`, `pin_eu=24h`, `fallback_order` field.

leo: Matrix uploaded to the runbook: https://go/runbooks/nova-13b-v3-dep-matrix. I've also added the exact fallback_order JSON snippet for the catalog entry.

aj: Dedicated-cap toggle tested in staging — ops flag `use_reserved_pool=true` will work. I'll attach the ops runbook snippet.

oncall-sre: Automated rollback policy is in place for the run. I added the monitoring alerts and a PagerDuty escalation policy in the deploy metadata.

anika: Thanks all. I'll kick off the deploy job 45m before the window for prewarm. If anything changes we'll update this thread. :rocket:

maria: LGTM. We'll hold on the enable step if the reranker hold is active.

leo: Minor doc note — if we hit the safety-hold, deploybot will keep rollout in 'paused' state and require manual `resume` from the release owner.

anika: Copy. Closing prep, will post a short post-deploy checklist here after the run.
